waivers.text:
SLEEPER — same board as Tuesday since none of last week's targets have been claimed yet. TE depth is still your #1 problem (Strange is your only rostered TE and shares Week 7's bye cluster with Herbert, Hampton, and your DEF), and Chase Brown insurance still matters since he starts in BOTH your leagues. FAAB: $93 left (spent $7 on Kmet/Vele/Shough claims already), waiver position 11 of 12 — doesn't matter much under FAAB, just get bids in before Wednesday's clear.
1. Samaje Perine (RB, CIN) — still unclaimed, still the direct Chase Brown handcuff anchoring your RB1 slot in both leagues. Drop Michael Wilson (WR, buried behind Marvin Harrison Jr./Trey McBride in ARI). FAAB $14.
2. Mike Gesicki (TE, CIN) — still available, still the best TE upgrade on the wire and it solves your zero-depth problem outright. Cincinnati's bye (Week 6) doesn't overlap Strange's Week 7. Drop Cole Kmet (TE, no clear role in CHI's rotation). FAAB $16.
3. Kimani Vidal (RB, LAC) — direct committee-mate to your own Omarion Hampton; cheap bye/injury insurance on a player who's already your RB1. Drop Woody Marks (RB, buried in Houston's committee). FAAB $8.
4. Evan Engram (TE, DEN) — fallback if you miss on Gesicki, or a second TE for bye coverage (Denver's bye is Week 10, different from both Strange's Week 7 and Gesicki's Week 6). No fixed drop unless you land both TEs — then cut whichever bench piece you value least. FAAB $6.
5. Devin Singletary (RB, NYG) — speculative depth add only if you whiff on the RBs above; lowest priority. No fixed drop, conditional pickup. FAAB $3.
No DEF/K stream needed this week — Aubrey and the Jaguars D/ST both carry playable Week 2 matchups per the Analysis tab.

trades.text:
SLEEPER — send Tyler Shough (New Orleans' actual Week 1 starting QB, currently buried as your QB2 behind Herbert) to Emeka Eggbucock ("Emeka Eggbucock") for Kaelon Black (RB, SF). Their starter Kyler Murray is in the concussion protocol — still day-to-day as of this run, with Carson Wentz starting if he can't go — and they're carrying zero backup QB, so a hot streaming starter has real short-term value to them. They're deep at RB (Ashton Jeanty, Tony Pollard, Javonte Williams, and Black all rostered), so Black is a fair piece to deal from that surplus. For you, Black is a legitimate stash: he out-touched Christian McCaffrey in the second half of Week 1 (15 total touches, tied for the team lead) and Draft Sharks already has him "pulling away" in San Francisco's RB2 race — real insurance and potential standalone value behind a back the 49ers want to manage carefully after a 450-touch 2025. This directly fixes your thinnest bench spot (Woody Marks, a committee back in Houston, is your only other RB depth) without touching Stefon Diggs, who's still starting regardless of the Flowers situation. Checked Weeks 15-17 first: moving a buried backup QB for a real RB stash only helps your playoff bench, it doesn't cost you anything there. Offer hasn't been accepted yet as of this run — still pending.
